# Arista EOS — GUI ↔ CLI ↔ SNMP Mapping

Per [gui-cli-snmp-unification.md](../../00-architecture/gui-cli-snmp-unification.md): every GUI action must be traceable to literal CLI text (echoed into the terminal) and, where a genuine SNMP SET path exists, that path documented explicitly rather than assumed.

**Headline finding**: given Arista's confirmed "all MIB support is read-only unless otherwise noted" posture (see [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md)), with only `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus` and `IF-MIB::ifAlias` confirmed writable, **the overwhelming majority of GUI actions on an Arista device have no realistic SNMP SET path and must be routed through the live CLI session.** This is a legitimate, documented finding — SignalScope's GUI should mark these actions "CLI-only" for Arista rather than exposing an SNMP-fallback affordance that doesn't actually work.

| GUI Action | CLI as echoed in terminal | SNMP SET (MIB::object, OID) | Read-back / GUI sync source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable port | `interface Ethernet1`<br>`no shutdown` | `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus.<ifIndex> = up(1)` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.7`) | `IF-MIB::ifOperStatus` (read-only, `.8`) via GET, or `show interfaces status` | One of only two confirmed EOS SNMP write paths. CLI is still the SignalScope-preferred path per architecture (session-based, not side-channel) when a live session exists; SNMP SET is a legitimate fallback here specifically because it's confirmed writable. |
| Disable port | `interface Ethernet1`<br>`shutdown` | `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus.<ifIndex> = down(2)` | Same as above | Same as above. |
| Set port description | `interface Ethernet1`<br>`description <text>` | `IF-MIB::ifAlias.<ifIndex>` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18`) | `show interfaces description` or `IF-MIB::ifAlias` GET | Confirmed writable — the other of the two known exceptions. |
| Configure access VLAN | `interface Ethernet1`<br>`switchport mode access`<br>`switchport access vlan 10` | No confirmed SNMP write path. `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qPvid` is the conceptual object but Arista's Q-BRIDGE-MIB support is listed read-only with no exception noted. | `show interfaces status`, `show vlan`, or `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qPvid` GET | **CLI-only.** Do not offer an SNMP fallback for this action on Arista. |
| Configure trunk allowed-VLANs | `interface Ethernet1`<br>`switchport mode trunk`<br>`switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30` | No confirmed SNMP write path. `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticEgressPorts`/`dot1qVlanStaticUntaggedPorts` are the conceptual objects, unconfirmed as writable on EOS. | `show interfaces trunk`, `show running-config section interface`, or `Q-BRIDGE-MIB` table GET | **CLI-only.** |
| Enable/disable spanning-tree PortFast | `interface Ethernet1`<br>`spanning-tree portfast` (or `no spanning-tree portfast`) | No confirmed SNMP write path; standard BRIDGE-MIB is read-only on EOS and has no PortFast-equivalent object regardless (PortFast is a non-standard IEEE concept). | `show spanning-tree interface Ethernet1 detail` or `show running-config section interface` | **CLI-only.** No standard MIB object represents PortFast even conceptually. |
| Configure LACP port-channel membership | `interface Ethernet1`<br>`channel-group 10 mode active` | No confirmed SNMP write path. IEEE8023-LAG-MIB (`dot3adAggPortListPorts` etc.) is the conceptual standard MIB but not confirmed supported/writable on EOS this session. | `show port-channel summary`, `show lacp interface` | **CLI-only.** |
| Port security (enable / set max MACs) | `interface Ethernet1`<br>`switchport port-security`<br>`switchport port-security mac-address maximum 4` | No confirmed SNMP write path; no standard or Arista enterprise MIB for port-security was confirmed writable this session. | `show port-security` (exact show-command name not independently confirmed this session — verify against a live device) | **CLI-only.** Exact CLI flag syntax itself is secondary-sourced (see [cli-reference.md](cli-reference.md) caveat) — verify before generating in production. |
| Save / persist configuration | `write memory` (or `copy running-config startup-config`) | No SNMP write path confirmed. Arista's `ARISTA-CONFIG-COPY-MIB`/`ARISTA-CONFIG-MAN-MIB` exist by name (analogous to Cisco's `CISCO-CONFIG-COPY-MIB` config-export trigger) but no confirmed SET-based save/copy trigger was found this session. | `show running-config` vs. last-known `show startup-config` diff (config-drift detection tier, see [connectivity-methods.md](../../00-architecture/connectivity-methods.md)) | **CLI-only pending further research.** If `ARISTA-CONFIG-COPY-MIB` does expose a SET-triggered copy action, this row should be revised — flagged as an open question, not asserted either way. |
| Configure SNMP community | `snmp-server community <string> [view <view>] [ro\|rw]` | N/A — this action *configures the SNMP agent itself*; there is no meaningful "SNMP SET to configure SNMP" loop (and SNMP-CONF/USM-related MIBs are conventionally not exposed for self-reconfiguration). | `show snmp community` / `show running-config section snmp` | Always CLI-only by nature of the action, independent of Arista's general posture. |
| Configure SNMP trap host | `snmp-server host <ip> [informs\|traps] version {1\|2c\|3} <community-or-user>` | N/A, same reasoning as above. | `show snmp host` / `show running-config section snmp` | CLI-only by nature. |

## Summary for SignalScope's capability matrix

Of the nine device-config actions above, only **two** (`ifAdminStatus` enable/disable and `ifAlias` description) have a confirmed, documented SNMP SET path on Arista EOS. Every VLAN, spanning-tree, LACP, port-security, and config-persistence action is CLI-only. This should be reflected directly in [comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md](../../comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md) as a narrow-write-surface vendor, consistent with the "all MIB support is read-only unless otherwise noted" statement from Arista's own documentation. SignalScope's per-device capability detection should not infer broader SNMP write support from the presence of an `rw` community string or `write`-mapped SNMPv3 view — as noted in [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md), that only grants access; it doesn't imply the underlying object accepts SET.
